text:
Hello, and welcome.

# Hello A single static page. No build step, no dependencies. It renders one centered greeting — "Hello, and welcome." — on a dark background, and nothing else. The favicon is a white "H" on a rounded square in the same dark colour as the page. ## Files | Path | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | The whole page — markup and inline styles | | `favicon.svg` | Favicon for modern browsers | | `favicon.ico` | Fallback favicon for browsers that ignore the SVG | ## Run it locally Open the file directly: ```sh open index.html ``` Or serve it over HTTP, which matches production more closely: ```sh python3 -m http.server 8000 # then visit http://localhost:8000 ``` ## Deploy Live at **https://suleimansh.github.io/test-project/** Deployment is GitHub Pages, driven by `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`. Every push to `main` publishes the site; it can also be run by hand from the Actions tab. One-time setup is already done on `suleimansh/test-project`: the remote exists and the Pages source is set to GitHub Actions (**Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source: GitHub Actions**). A fresh fork or clone needs both steps repeated before its first deploy will publish. Because this is a *project* Pages site, it is served from the `/test-project/` subpath rather than the domain root. Asset links in `index.html` are therefore relative (`favicon.ico`, not `/favicon.ico`) — a root-absolute path resolves to `suleimansh.github.io/favicon.ico` and 404s. The workflow copies only `index.html`, `favicon.ico`, and `favicon.svg` into the published artifact. The repository root is *not* deployed wholesale — anything not in that list (for example `.the-framework/`, which holds internal run logs and analysis notes) is never reachable from the public site. If you add a file that should be served, add it to the `Stage site` step or it will not ship. .github/workflows: deploy.yml .openagent: 2026-10-14T05-21-57-347Z.json 2026-10-14T05-21-57-347Z.jsonl .the-framework: ANALYSIS_RESULT.md LOGS.md synced
